items.title: Eddie Metz Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 3, 2015
items.q: He’s one of my heroes, but I did hear those things

ctx.x: And he basically told the same thing. He says Freddie, he says, if the time starts to get away he would just look at you.

Yeah. He didn’t tolerate it. And yet I heard on Basie records with Sonny Payne near the end of his career with the band, he and Freddie were fighting all the time. You can hear it a couple of times on “Sinatra Live at the Sands.” There’s a couple of times. The set that the Basie band played before Frank Sinatra came out. The dinner set. So you can hear all the silverware clanking and a guy yelling, “waiter.” And maybe the mob guys sitting down front because, you know, Frank was there. “Hey bring me my food” you…
Was Sonny like on the forward side of the beat?
